requirements.description: Compustat annual fundamentals for realized historical training earnings and predictors: income before extraordinary items, assets, dividends and derived indicators, and accruals constructed with the source-stated pre-/post-1988 methods.

required_coverage.frequency: Annual Compustat observations by fiscal-year label/date
required_coverage.population: Cross-sectional annual observations at the CRSP/Compustat intersection for NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq listed securities with share codes 10 or 11, excluding ADRs, closed-end funds, and REITs.
required_coverage.detail: Raw inputs belong to the historical coefficient-training samples at forecast origins 1968–2008; all must be available at the respective origin. The paper states ten-year training histories and source data starting in 1963 but does not reconcile the early origins or precisely define the training-window endpoints. The earliest necessary year remains null. A future forecast horizon is not a requirement for realized post-2008 training data. Local historical/population coverage remains unconfirmed.

routes.mapping_notes: Catalog labels support `at` (total assets), `ib` (income before extraordinary items), `act`, `che`, `lct`, `dlc`, `txp`, `dp`, and `oancf` for the stated measures. The paper does not identify the Compustat dividend item; `dv`, `dvc`, and `dvt` are live candidates, so the exact dividend mapping and payer coding remain unverified. Compustat field units/vintage and year-t versus fyear alignment also need confirmation.

variable_coverage.construction: Read Compustat income before extraordinary items (`ib`) at year t+τ for the result-set horizon (τ=1, 2, or 3); retain the stated $m scale and annual 1/99 winsorization. The source does not resolve Compustat field units or the annual t-to-fyear mapping.
Use Compustat total assets (`at`) at year t, in the paper’s $m scale and annual 1/99 winsorization.
Use the Compustat dividend-payment measure at year t. The article does not name the exact Compustat item; `dv`, `dvc`, and `dvt` are available candidates, so preserve this mapping as unresolved.

Derive the dividend-payer indicator at year t from the selected dividend measure. The paper defines 1 for dividend payers and 0 otherwise but does not specify the exact dividend item or threshold/missing-value rule.
Use Compustat income before extraordinary items (`ib`) at year t, in the paper’s $m scale and annual 1/99 winsorization.
Derive the negative-earnings indicator as 1 when the year-t earnings measure is negative and 0 otherwise; use the same earnings definition as the RHS earnings variable.

Before 1988, compute Δ(non-cash current assets) − Δ(current liabilities excluding short-term debt and taxes payable) − depreciation/amortization using Compustat `act`, `che`, `lct`, `dlc`, `txp`, `dp`; from 1988, compute `ib` − `oancf`. Retain $m units and annual 1/99 winsorization.

design_coverage.reason: No clustered standard-error dimension is reported for the annual pooled fits; Table 1 separately reports Newey–West inference over yearly coefficient estimates.
Equation (1) reports no fixed-effect dimensions; no additional data requirement is introduced.
No regression weights are reported in Equation (1); no separate input is introduced.

implementation_issues.description: The paper calls Equation (1) a pooled cross-sectional regression but does not name the annual estimator. The linear equation alone does not identify OLS or another estimator.
Table 1 applies Newey–West inference to the annual coefficient estimates but does not report the lag/bandwidth or finite-sample correction needed to reproduce the reported t-statistics.

The paper names Compustat dividends without specifying the item; the local catalog has distinct dividend candidates (`dv`, `dvc`, `dvt`). The precise payer threshold and missing/zero coding for DD are also not stated.

The target sample is the CRSP/Compustat intersection, but the article does not report GVKEY–PERMNO link-selection rules. Available CCM type, primary-link, and date fields provide a route but leave the sample mapping unresolved.

The source states ten-year historical fits at forecast origins 1968–2008 but declares source intervals beginning in 1963; early-window treatment and exact training endpoints are unresolved. Its strict out-of-sample requirement rules out treating the three-year target forecast as a realized 2011 training outcome. Preserve unknown earliest raw dates rather than imposing an unsupported 1957–2011 requirement. This is a specification/coverage uncertainty, not an access barrier.

Equation (1) denotes annual observations by t but does not specify whether t is a calendar year or Compustat fiscal-year label, nor how datadate/fyear are aligned to CRSP months for the sample intersection.

review_notes: Table 1 reports 41 annual coefficient fits per horizon (1968–2008), averaged across years; the model-based forecast applications and later ICC analyses are outside this frozen baseline.
The reported annual source intervals do not prove local historical coverage. Exact local probes establish only current access and field presence.

Earnings is income before extraordinary items from
Compustat.
evidence.description: Paper maps earnings to Compustat income before extraordinary items.

evidence.quote: Total assets and dividends are also from Compustat.
evidence.description: Paper identifies Compustat as the source of assets and dividends, without naming exact items.

evidence.description: Paper specifies annual 1st/99th percentile winsorization for earnings and other level variables.

evidence.quote:
Prior to 1988, accruals are calculated using the balance sheet
method as the change in non-cash current assets less the change in current liabilities excluding the change in short-term debt and the change in taxes
payable minus depreciation and amortization expense.
evidence.description: Paper defines the pre-1988 balance-sheet accrual method, requiring current and prior annual balances.

evidence.quote:
Starting in 1988, accruals are calculated using the cash flow statement method as the difference
between earnings and cash flows from operations.
evidence.description: Paper defines accruals from 1988 onward as earnings less operating cash flows.

evidence.quote:
We correct for serial dependence by applying the Newey-West
procedure to the annual coefficient estimates
evidence.description: Paper applies Newey–West inference to the annual coefficient estimates, without specifying a bandwidth here.

evidence.quote:
This is to ensure that our earnings forecasts are strictly out of sample (that is, all information
that is required to forecast earnings for years tþ1 through tþ5 is available in year t).
evidence.description: Training inputs and realized training outcomes must be available at the forecast origin; future target earnings are forecasts, not future observations required to fit the historical coefficients.

review_notes: The frozen baseline is Equation (1), with Table 1 one-, two-, and three-year-ahead coefficient averages; horizons four and five are not tabulated and are not added as fits.

Coordinator source review distinguishes forecast-origin years from historical regression-row years. Strict out-of-sample estimation does not need realized earnings after the latest forecast origin; the source-declared start and early ten-year history remain unresolved. The corrected audit keeps earliest raw bounds null and does not change the frozen baseline fit IDs.
Current COMP.FUNDA, CRSP.MSF, CRSP.DSENAMES, and CCM exact-resource probes establish current access/fields only. They do not confirm historical coverage for the specified population.
The Compustat annual map is incomplete for dividends and annual year alignment; the local field labels identify candidate variables but do not establish the exact paper mapping or data vintage.
